finding.claim: Open redirect: with redirect:true and default prefix '/', a GET to /.//<dirname> makes getRedirectUrl return a '//<dirname>/' Location header, so the browser navigates to host <dirname>. The host must be an existing directory name under the served root.
finding.source: Unauthenticated HTTP GET path /.//<name> (index.js:137-154, wildcard route /* since prefix defaults to '/' at index.js:72).

trace.note: createRoutePrefixMatcher returns 0 for prefix '/', so pathname = '/.//<name>'
send() resolves ./<name> under root; directory -> type 'directory' (relies on @fastify/send, not readable)
redirect branch only when opts.redirect === true
getRedirectUrl strips leading '/' and '\\' only, then prepends one '/'
new URL('/.//<name>', 'http://localhost.com/') parses to pathname '//<name>' (WHATWG behaviour, from spec, not executed)
returns '//<name>/' plus search; no check rejects a leading '//'

finding.guards_checked: getRedirectUrl (index.js:783-799) has no rejection of pathnames beginning '//'. Traversal checks at index.js:262 and index.js:769 only cover '..' segments. The prefix !== opts.prefix branch (index.js:155) does not apply with prefix '/'. Impact limited: redirect default is off, and host must be an existing directory name in the root (e.g. attacker-uploaded directory). Trick not executed; based on reading and WHATWG URL spec.

finding.claim: Existence oracle: with preCompressed:true, a request for /../<dir>/ with an Accept-Encoding header gets 404 if <dir>/index.html does not exist outside the root, and 403 if it does. This leaks existence of index.html files outside the served root. No content is disclosed.
finding.source: Unauthenticated HTTP GET /../<dir>/ with Accept-Encoding header (leading '..' permitted at index.js:262-263; encoding negotiated at index.js:280).
finding.sink: findIndexFile at index.js:284 (path.join + statSync at index.js:586-588), oracle observable via response code at index.js:285-288 and send 403 at index.js:302.

trace.note: findIndexFile(pathname, root, options.index) stats path.join(root, pathname, 'index.html'), which can escape root
if no index file found -> callNotFound (404)
send rejects leading '..' with 403 (relies on @fastify/send, not readable)

finding.guards_checked: Leading '..' is deliberately permitted at index.js:262-263; containment is enforced only inside send after the stat, so findIndexFile has no containment check. Without preCompressed the response is always 403 and no oracle exists. Impact is an existence oracle for index.html outside root only; no content disclosure. The 403 comes from @fastify/send, which was not readable.
